items.title: Sid Davilla Interview, 1969-04-17
items.q: Matter of fact, there's a friend of mine over there, there are two Costa boys in town who have been musicians for years. One is Tony Costa and one is Mike Costa.

ctx.x: He had his big success of him, about three years, three success of him, tours. Oh, they loved him. They loved him. They loved him.

Now they, a number of New Orleans musicians have made Japan their home, you know. Matter of fact, I had a few tempting offers to go over there, teach in the schools and play music. And like the money was adequate, you know. Matter of fact, there's a friend of mine over there, there are two Costa boys in town who have been musicians for years. One is Tony Costa and one is Mike Costa. Excellent musicians. What do you think now about the future of Bourbon Street in general? What do you think there? I mean, it's of…

changing? For instance, like these new motels, hotels they're building here, they've got three new ones in the last few years. I don't know what's going to happen to Bourbon Street, Tom, because it's been a busy street, and it's a lot busier on the outside than it is on the inside, actually, when you read the register in the morning. That's true.
